content: The medication balsalazide may cause side effects such as headache, nausea, vomiting, joint pain, diarrhea, abdominal pain, fever, sore throat, difficulty sleeping, or loss of appetite. It is important to remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the potential risks of side effects. In rare cases, balsalazide may worsen ulcerative colitis. Severe allergic reactions to this medication are uncommon. This is not an exhaustive list of possible side effects. If you are in the United States or Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice regarding side effects. Before taking balsalazide, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other aminosalicylates (such as mesalamine or olsalazine), to salicylates (such as aspirin or salsalate), or to sulfasalazine. Additionally, disclose any other allergies you may have. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other issues. Balsalazide may increase your sensitivity to sunlight, particularly if you have skin conditions like atopic dermatitis or eczema. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen and protective clothing when outdoors. This medication contains sodium and is chemically similar to aspirin. Children and teenagers under 18 years of age should not take aspirin if they have chickenpox, the flu, an undiagnosed illness, or have recently received a vaccine. During pregnancy, balsalazide should only be used when clearly necessary. It may also pass into breast milk, so consult your doctor if you are breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal supplements, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Balsalazide is very similar to mesalamine and may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine normetanephrine levels, potentially causing false test results. In the event of an overdose, if the individual has serious symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. While taking this medication, your doctor may order laboratory or medical tests, such as kidney and liver function tests, to monitor your condition. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store balsalazide at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. For further guidance, consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for individualized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
